newsitem.title: UK: NSM slumps, says in talks with banks.
newsitem.headline: NSM slumps, says in talks with banks.

text.p: Shares in mining group NSM Plc almost halved in value on Thursday after the company warned that it expected to make a loss in the half year ended September 30 and said it was in talks with its banks.
The stock was marked down 19-1/2p at 23p by 0855 GMT though no trading was recorded.
NSM said in a statement it planned to sell its U.S. operations and had appointed investment bank PaineWebber Inc. to carry out the sale.

"It is expected that this sale will be a substantial discount to net asset value," said the company, adding that it also planned to sell other assets. It forecast a loss in the half-year ending September 30.
"The company is in discusssion with its bankers regarding its immediate short-term working capital requirements and its capital structure following the proposed disposal," it added.

Following the planned sale of its U.S. businesses and other disposals of non-core assets already under negotiation, NSM said it would end up being "principally based in South Wales, supported by opencast mining operations in England and Scotland."
